name: online billing service – For online stores
author: onlinebilling

sections.description:
Using our plugin you can issue invoices and send them to your clients from your online shop dashboard.
Invoices will be generated on online-billing-service.com website in your account.

Our plugin is relying on a 3rd party as a service, we are collecting some data from your website through our API in order to generate invoices.
Website link: online-billing-service.com
Terms and conditions
Privacy policy and GDPR

online-billing-service.com

A few notes about the sections above:

  • “Contributors” onlinebilling
  • “Tags” v1.7.1
  • “Requires at least” WordPress version 6.7.
  • “Tested up to” WordPress version 6.9.

Installing

  1. Upload online_billing_service in /wp-content/plugins/ directory.
  2. Activate plugin from ‘Plugins’ tab from your WordPress dashboard.
  3. Login with api_key generated on online-billing-service.com.
  4. You can configure plugin from Settings tab.

Or you can install our plugin directly from WordPress dashboard from Plugins section.

Arbitrary section

We are using GraphQL API provided by online-billing-service.com.
sections.faq:
How can I change the invoice state?

The default state of an invoice is issued but from settings you can check the document state box and next generated invoices will have
the draft state.

Is there a usage limit for the plugin?

The plugin works through the online-billing-service.com API, so it is limited by your plan’s API request quota (per hour, per day and per month). The quota differs from plan to plan. A single operation, such as invoicing an order, can use several requests.

Once the limit is reached, requests are refused until the quota frees up. In the meantime no invoices are issued, and the WordPress admin shows the limit message received from online-billing-service.com. Orders left without an invoice can be invoiced later from the orders list or from the order page.

If your plan has limits, they are shown in your account, on the WooCommerce integration page. For a larger quota, upgrade your plan.

How can I customise the invoice data from my theme or plugin (hooks)?

The plugin exposes WordPress filters (apply_filters) at the key points, applied before the data is escaped and sent to online-billing-service.com:

  • online_billing_service_invoice_product_name( $product_name, $item, $product, $order ) – product line name
  • online_billing_service_invoice_product_code( $product_code, $item, $product, $order ) – product line code (SKU)
  • online_billing_service_invoice_shipping_name( $shipping_name, $order ) – shipping line name
  • online_billing_service_invoice_fee_name( $fee_name, $fee_item, $order ) – fee line name
  • online_billing_service_client_name( $client_name, $order ) – client name on the invoice
  • action online_billing_service_invoice_created( $document_id, $order, $document_type, $reversed_document_id ) – runs after the document was created and recorded on the order ($document_type is invoice or proformaInvoice)

Example (in your theme’s functions.php):

add_filter( 'online_billing_service_invoice_product_name', function ( $name, $item, $product, $order ) { return $product ? $product->get_sku() . ' - ' . $name : $name; }, 10, 4 );
sections.changelog:
Ready to deploy!

1.7.1

  • The logo on the plugin pages shows again, at a fitting size
  • The description names the WordPress version the plugin requires, 6.7

1.7.0

  • The checkout asks whether the buyer is an individual or a company, and a company’s name, VAT ID and registration number, which go on the invoice – on the checkout block (WooCommerce 9.9 or newer) and on the classic checkout, in the shop’s language (English or German)
  • The order screen has the same fields on every order, also on one created there, to fill in or correct before invoicing
  • A checkout where another plugin already asks for the VAT ID: the settings name its fields and leave these off, so buyers are not asked twice, and the invoices take the VAT ID and registration number that plugin saves, where they can be recognised
  • Declared compatible with WooCommerce’s own order tables (HPOS) and the checkout block

1.6.10

  • Fee lines (e.g. a cash on delivery fee) are invoiced at the VAT rate WooCommerce charged on them, no longer at the rate of the order’s last product
  • Invoices, their series and payments are dated by the shop’s time zone, not UTC (orders invoiced after midnight in Romania got the day before)

1.6.9

  • Bumped version for trademark compliance and readme updates

1.6.9

  • update company buyer name settings

0.9.8

  • fix vat bug, added company name label

0.9.7

  • generic fallback client exists function

0.9.6

  • fix bugs with client identification in client_exists

0.9.5

  • fix bug price divided by zero

0.9.4

  • fix bug with float string conversion for product lines

0.9.1

  • tested up to WordPress version 6.9

0.9.0

  • fix all proforma_invoices generation known bugs
